summary: Module 03 (en) technical review done. I recomputed every equation, worked example, check, exercise solution and quiz answer. I ran every code block in 10-*, 11-*, 12-* and 30-* in the lab environment, and all 18 blocks reproduce their printed outputs; e14's marching-cubes lines need scikit-image 0.26, which I installed into a private directory to run them. I recomputed by independent scripts: the s13 disc, sphere and ellipsoid measurements; MobileNet's 569 M and 149 M MACs and its 95% pointwise share; the separable SmallResNet's 187,018 parameters and per-stage counts; LeNet's 340,908 connections; the 11-point AP of 0.682; the ERF mass (0.44 in 9x9, 0.53 in 11x11, 0.89 in 25x25); and the blur and sharpen outputs. I checked the ConvNeXt Table 10 and Table 1 values against the paper's PDF: every row is correct to 0.1, and 81.97 +/- 0.06 is confirmed. Every number the concept text quotes from Labs 1-6 matches the printed lab outputs. A rough re-run of Lab 2's augmentation try-this experiments gave the same direction and similar size as s10's quoted runs: 0.93 to 0.85, 0.36 to 0.71 and 0.77 to 0.92, against the quoted 0.90 to 0.83, 0.36 to 0.66 and 0.76 to 0.90. All cross-module links point at the right sections (M01 s8/s10, M02 s2/s3/s6/s8/s10/s11, M04 e15, M06 s5/s8/s11, M10 s2). The CANONICAL M03 notes are applied: ViT is only a pointer, e1 is graded two stars, Lab 4 uses five seeds, the norun extensions are in place and the M04 e15 reference is correct. No public-site violations were found. Exercise budget: 7 one-star, 7 two-star and 1 three-star exercises, 130 minutes. Each quiz question has exactly one defensible answer. Fixes by kind: 4 factual or citation, 1 provenance, 3 exercise solutions, 4 quiz explanations (12 in all), plus 3 lab issues reported. node tools/check.mjs --module 3 --lang en reports 0 errors and 0 warnings.
changes: 11-concepts-b.md s6 (1x1 convolution): 'Lin et al. (2014) built a whole network from such layers ("Network in Network")' -> 'Lin et al. (2014) followed every spatial convolution with a stack of such layers, a small MLP at each pixel ("Network in Network")'. NIN interleaves spatial convolutions with 1x1 (mlpconv) layers; it is not built from 1x1 layers alone.

11-concepts-b.md s7 (LeNet-5): 'A system built on this network read bank cheques for a decade.' -> 'A cheque-reading system built on this network was deployed commercially in the mid-1990s.' The duration claim had no source, and BRIEF says to give fewer details rather than uncertain ones.

11-concepts-b.md s7 (VGG): 'and the networks have 16 to 19 weight layers' -> 'and the networks it compares have 11 to 19 weight layers, of which VGG-16 and VGG-19 are the ones still in use'. The paper's configurations A-E span 11 to 19 weight layers.
12-concepts-c.md s11 (IoU): 'PASCAL VOC counts a detection as a true positive if its IoU ... is at least 0.5' -> '... exceeds 0.5'. VOC's criterion is overlap greater than 50%.

12-concepts-c.md s13 worked example 'Measuring ideal shapes': 'NumPy and contourpy, centres at a sub-pixel offset.' -> 'NumPy and contourpy, with the centre offset from a pixel centre by (0.2, 0.2) pixels for the disc and from a voxel centre by (0.3, 0.3, 0.3) voxels for the spheres.' These offsets reproduce every quoted number (201 pixels, 64, 52.9, 50.2; 4,199 voxels, 1,884 faces; ratios 1.51/1.50/1.50). Other offsets give different counts, e.g. 200 or 4,189.

30-exercises.md e1(b): 'Rows 1, 3 and 5 are read twice ...; rows 0 and 6 are read once.' -> '...; rows 0, 2, 4 and 6 are read once.' The code's output [1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1] shows rows 2 and 4 are also read once.

30-exercises.md e2(c): 'At n = 100 the stack uses 2.2% of the weights (9/400 = 2.25% is the asymptote).' -> '... 2.2% of the weights, close to the approximation 9/400 = 2.25%.' 9/(4n) is an approximation that tends to 0, not an asymptote.

30-exercises.md e6(c): 'The residual network is not immune to the opposite fault: the gradient can still grow if the epsilon_i are consistently positive, which is why the 55-layer residual network with batch norm in Section 8 has a stem gradient of about 0.8 and not exactly 1.' -> 'The residual network is not immune to drift: if the epsilon_i share a sign, the product still moves away from 1 geometrically (the 7.24 and 0.133 of part (b)), only far more slowly than a plain stack's. Section 8's 55-layer networks with batch norm show the contrast: a stem gradient of about 190 for the plain network against 0.8 with shortcuts.' The old sentence used a value below 1 as evidence of growth, and a gradient norm is not a gain factor.

40-practice.md quiz Q2 explanation: '63 is what a kernel of width 2 would give, a sign that the dilation was ignored' was wrong (k = 2, p = 1 gives 65). It now reads: 64 is also what ignoring the dilation gives (64 + 2 - 2 - 1 + 1), and '63 ignores the dilation and also drops the final +1, 64 + 2 - 2 - 1 = 63'.

40-practice.md quiz Q4 explanation: '11 comes from forgetting that the jump doubles after the stride' was wrong (forgetting the doubling gives 9). It now reads: '11 applies the doubled jump to the third layer only and lets the fourth add 2 again (3, 5, 9, 11), forgetting that the jump stays doubled for every later layer.'

40-practice.md quiz Q9 explanation: 'two real objects that overlap above the threshold are merged into one detection' -> 'of two real objects that overlap above the threshold, the lower-scoring one is deleted'. NMS deletes boxes; it does not merge them.

40-practice.md quiz Q11 explanation: 'The first option swaps the two quantities' -> 'The first option gives the foreground share as the accuracy, the second takes the Dice coefficient to equal the accuracy'. Option 1 does not swap anything, and option 2 was not explained.
issues: Lab 3 (20-labs-a.md), step 8 prose: 'in separate runs at peaks of 0.03 and 0.02 their 19-layer training loss was still about 0.9 and their 55-layer loss 1.7 to 1.9'. No lab code prints these numbers, yet s8 and the lab's 'What you should see' rely on them ('plain networks stay far behind at every rate tried'). Fix: add the plain networks to step 8's loop, e.g. train_depth(b, False, peak=peak, seed=s) for b in (9, 27) and s in range(3), and quote the printed values.

Lab 2 (20-labs-a.md), Try this 3: the epochs, seeds and test canvas are not specified, so s10's quoted '0.36 to 0.66 at 5 images per class, 0.76 to 0.90 at 20' (and Try this 2's '0.90 to 0.83') cannot be reproduced exactly. My re-run with 3 seeds, 200 or 300 epochs and batch 32 gave 0.93 to 0.85, 0.36 to 0.71 and 0.77 to 0.92: same direction, similar size. Fix: state the epochs, seeds and evaluation set in Try this 2 and 3 (e.g. '300 epochs, batch 32, seeds 0-2, evaluated on the step-6 test canvas'), or give each a code block whose output s10 can quote.
Lab 6 (21-labs-b.md), step 1 output: 'class balance: 0.5214999914169312' prints a raw float32. Fix the print to format the value as {:.3f}, giving 'class balance: 0.521', and update the output fence.

Not fixed: s13's anisotropic-ellipsoid worked example (semi-axes 12, 9, 7) quotes '6,372 voxels' 'at one sub-voxel placement' without saying which placement. My recomputation gives 6,369 at (0.3, 0.6, 0.2) and 6,371 at (0.2, 0.2, 0.2), so the figure is plausible but cannot be reproduced exactly. The other quoted values are reproduced: 20 placements with default_rng(0) give mean 3,169 and sd 30.8, exposed faces about 1,613, marching cubes 1,316.7 binary and 1,136.3 blurred. If a later pass wants exact provenance, name the offset and requote.
